paragraphs.tag: MAP: g-1 | dark Earth in space turns to Europe; title WWII · THE WAAL CROSSING
paragraphs.text: September, nineteen forty-four. Five years into the war, the Allies stake everything on one road through Holland, and on the bridges that carry it.

paragraphs.tag: MAP: g-2 | camera dives through the clouds onto 3D Holland: the road glows north, Eindhoven, Nijmegen, Arnhem; Nijmegen bridge pulses red
paragraphs.text: Sixty miles of road, running north to the Rhine. At Nijmegen, the great bridge over the Waal is still in German hands.

paragraphs.tag: ARCHIVE: f-1 | date card 20 SEPTEMBER 1944 · NIJMEGEN, HOLLAND; restored film: gliders, paratroopers, guns
paragraphs.text: For three days, the paratroopers of the eighty-second Airborne throw themselves at it. For three days, they are thrown back.

paragraphs.tag: ARCHIVE: f-2 | Gavin portrait (depth move), name card; restored film: boats carried to the river
paragraphs.text: Their commander, James Gavin, just thirty-seven years old, chooses the one way no one expects. Across the river. In daylight. In canvas boats.

paragraphs.tag: MAP: m-1 | dark 3D-lit tactical map: 26 boats push off from the south bank, German guns on the north bank fire, impacts in the water (shake), counter 26 BOATS · 260 MEN · 300 M OF OPEN WATER
paragraphs.text: Twenty-six boats. Two hundred and sixty men. Three hundred metres of open water, under the German guns.

paragraphs.tag: MAP: m-2 | about half the boats grey out; the rest reach the north bank; blue sweeps east to the bridge; bridge turns blue; end title
paragraphs.text: Half of the boats never reach the far side. The rest do. And by nightfall, the bridge is theirs.
